name: Unreadable Work
problem: A person cannot see what their AI is doing for them: whether background work is moving, or what an answer rests on.
who_has_it: People and teammates watching a live chat or a background run, and people who read an answer about their own goals, notes and decisions.
why_it_matters: A silent run looks like a failure, so people interrupt work that was going fine, repeat the request or give up, and a stuck run can go unnoticed. An answer whose path is hidden is harder to trust or correct than the same answer shown with the work behind it.
why_hard: What is shown has to be true to what the run did, so it cannot be invented; the same event stream suits a live viewer, a background milestone feed and a log; the trace of a turn is long and mostly noise; and an explanation a model writes can sound right and be wrong.
existing_attempts: Raw log tailing, spinners, per-step messages and a final summary only; progress sinks that show every event while a person watches and milestones once the run is in the background; interim replies for an attempt that did not meet the goal; the work trace shown beside a reply; linking sources.

name: Parts Pass While The Assistant Fails
problem: Each part of QAR can pass its own test while the assistant, as a person meets it across a day, forgets what it knows, acts unasked, claims work it did not do, or answers a vague request with a generic plan, and the person is the one who finds out.
who_has_it: People who use Quest AI as their everyday assistant, and the maintainers who judge it part by part.
why_it_matters: Trust in an assistant is lost by a single surprise: an email described as sent that was not, a delete with no question, an invented address. The person then checks everything it does, which removes the point of having it.
why_hard: The person's seat spans routing, context, planning, acting and answering, so no single part's metric sees the failure; the requirements are many and several, such as nudging unprompted or lasting over sessions, take more than a single message to score.
existing_attempts: Per-part metrics, the chat-quality cases on a dev account, and a small set of day-with-assistant end-to-end cases (a morning briefing, a spoken note, ask-first email and calendar, a background hand-off, a refusal, a delete held for confirmation) scored from the world afterwards and the reply.
